title: The India Way (Vienna) — Eric speaks on 'Caring for the Golden Goose' at the Living Machine Institute session ahead of the Global Peter Drucker Forum
summary: Erika Clegg, leadership and communications adviser and author of Junk Values, announces she will be at The India Way in Vienna on 3 November at the invitation of Living Machine Institute founder Unni Krishnan, and that Eric is on the programme with a talk titled 'Caring for the Golden Goose'. The session is devoted to institutional longevity and closes with contributions to a Vienna Declaration on the subject; Harish Bhat speaks on Ratan Tata's leadership legacy. The Global Peter Drucker Forum runs 4–5 November at the Hofburg with pre-events on the 3rd. Programme detail is from Clegg's announcement — the Living Machine Institute's own page had not been updated for 2026 at the time of writing.
blockquote:
On 3 November I’ll be at The India Way in Vienna with the Living Machine Institute,Living Machine Institute, by kind invitation of its founder Unni Krishnan. It’s part of the Global Peter Drucker Forum and devoted to the idea of institutional longevity.

Unni’s central question is essentially this: what allows an organisation to become something greater and more enduring than the people who happen to be running it at any particular moment?

We’ll hear Eric Ries on Caring for the Golden Goose and Harish Bhat on Ratan Tata’s leadership legacy, before contributing to the Vienna Declaration on Institutional Longevity.
